subject: English Language
sourceFile: Copy of English Studies BECE Syllabus - syllabusNG.txt
examFormat: The syllabus assesses candidates' proficiency in reading, comprehending and analyzing passages, their listening and speaking skills, and their ability to analyze and appreciate literary texts, building a foundation for post-basic English. Paper 1 (Language) has 80 multiple-choice questions in 80 minutes for 80 marks: Section A Comprehension (two passages with five questions each or one passage with ten), Section B Vocabulary Development (25 questions), Section C Grammatical Accuracy (30 questions) and Section D Spoken English (15 questions). Paper 2 (Literature) has 40 multiple-choice questions in 40 minutes for 40 marks: five questions from each of the three drama and three prose texts and ten from poetry. Paper 3 (Language, Essay) lasts 45 minutes with two compulsory questions of 15 marks each (30 marks).
excluded: Syllabus.ng marketing ("About us", "About BECE"), eligibility, registration, grading table, table of contents and the FAQ chapter were left out. The "Vocabulary Development" topic is taken from the Paper 1 Section B description, since the syllabus table has no vocabulary theme. Prescribed literature texts (2020–2023) are listed as subtopics of three "Recommended" topics; the secondary text and poetry anthologies are in recommendedTexts only.

topics.name: Reading for Main and Supporting Ideas
objectives: Identify main and supporting ideas in a given passage relating to sports, education and election.
Differentiate between main and supporting ideas/gists in a given passage.

topics.name: Reading to Follow Directions in Written Communication
objectives: Read to follow directions in written communication.
Identify key words in a passage that show direction.
Blend materials with related sketches.

topics.name: Reading for Meanings of Words in Various Contexts
objectives: Read for meanings of words in various contexts through clues provided by surrounding words.
Read for meanings of words in various contexts through alternative words that can fit into the context.

topics.name: Critical Reading
objectives: Explain the meaning and steps of critical reading.
Apply the critical process: surveying, skimming, line-by-line reading, recalling and reading.
Identify facts and opinions in a passage on the evils of cigarette smoking.

topics.name: Reading for Critical Evaluation
objectives: Read critically.
Explain the meaning, aspects and essence of critical reading.
Identify facts, opinions and deductions in selected passages on critical reading.
Explain the meaning of danger signs on our roads and the types of danger signs on the roads.

topics.name: Reading for Speed
objectives: Survey/scan for main points.
Skim for specific information.

topics.name: Reading for Summary
objectives: Identify topic sentences and key ideas in suitable passages/stories.
Identify expressions that redirect attention to the main points in passages on past content, types of communication and safe storage of food.

topics.name: Reading to Answer Specific Questions
objectives: Read selected passages carefully with the intention of answering questions on them at the knowledge, translation, interpretation and projection levels.

topics.name: Reading for Maximum Retention and Recall
objectives: Read for maximum recall.
Use reading strategies such as preview, question, recite, recall and review.

topics.name: Reading to Understand the Author's Mood
objectives: Identify the author's mood, e.g. anger, happiness, doubt, disappointment, suspicion and excitement.

topics.name: Reading for Spatial Description
objectives: Read for spatial description, e.g. interpretation of diagrams, maps and sketches.

topics.name: Reading to Understand the Writer's Purpose
objectives: Identify the writer's purpose(s), e.g. to persuade, inform, convince, irritate, annoy, please, entertain, dissuade, stimulate thought and indoctrinate.
Read selected passages on contemporary issues, e.g. inflation, HIV/AIDS, mobile communication and corruption.

topics.name: Vocabulary Development
objectives: Express thoughts, ideas, views, opinions and observations in English using vocabulary related to anchor points such as home, school, places of worship, market, health, education, government and youth empowerment.

Use vocabulary related to drug abuse, human rights, population and family life education, food safety, consumer protection, sexually transmitted diseases, peace education, gender issues, national values, road safety and environmental education.
topics.content: From the Paper 1 Section B description: expressing thoughts, ideas, views, opinions and observations in English using anchor points such as home, school, places of worship, market, health, education, government, youth empowerment, drug abuse, human rights, population and family life education, drug abuse education, food safety, consumer protection, sexually transmitted diseases, peace education, gender issues, national values, road safety and environmental education.

topics.name: Writing to Highlight Main and Supporting Ideas
objectives: Write a story or passage highlighting main and supporting ideas.
Arrange ideas in logical sequence with an introduction and conclusion.

topics.name: Composition Writing
objectives: Apply the elements of composition: introduction (pre-writing, writing and editing), body and conclusion.
Arrange ideas in logical sequence.
topics.content: Theme: Writing. Narrative, descriptive, expository and argumentative composition.

topics.name: Letter Writing
objectives: Distinguish between the types of letters: formal and informal.

subtopics.name: Formal letters
objectives: Identify the features of formal letters: two addresses, opening salutation, body of the letter, closing and signature.

subtopics.name: Informal letters
objectives: Identify the features of informal letters: one address, opening salutation, body of the letter and closing.

topics.name: Summary Writing
objectives: Write summaries from selected passages on contemporary issues.
Identify topic sentences from given paragraphs/passages.
Identify key ideas from different passages, e.g. passages on corruption and road accidents.

topics.name: Production of Vowel and Consonant Sounds
topics.content: Theme: Listening and speaking. Production of vowel and consonant sounds in passages.

subtopics.name: Vowel sounds
objectives: Produce vowel sounds in passages.

subtopics.name: Consonant sounds
objectives: Produce consonant sounds in passages.

subtopics.name: Long and short vowels
objectives: Distinguish long and short vowels, e.g. /æ/ back and /ɑː/ bark; bit/beat; hit/heat.

subtopics.name: Consonants and consonant clusters
objectives: Produce consonants (e.g. f/v in fish/van, few/love) and consonant clusters (e.g. respect, principle, struggle).

subtopics.name: Diphthongs
objectives: Produce diphthongs, e.g. /eɪ/, /aɪ/, /aʊ/.

topics.name: Intonation, Stress and Rhythm
objectives: Listen to speeches on human rights, gender issues, value orientation (honesty, respect for elders, punctuality, regularity, etc.), peace education, conflict resolution, drug abuse, global warming, road safety, security and inter-ethnic marriages.
Highlight correct intonation, stress and rhythm.
Make statements, commands and questions using the correct stress, intonation and rhythm.

topics.name: Listening Comprehension
objectives: Listen to and comprehend live or recorded speeches and materials on the family, the neighbourhood, accountability in government, infectious diseases, peace in the community and examination malpractice.
Listen to and comprehend speeches and materials on the environment, health issues, the computer, cultural practices, the school, election, and child labour and trafficking.
topics.content: Theme: Listening and speaking. Speeches and materials (live or recorded) on the family (nuclear and extended), the neighbourhood, accountability in government, infectious diseases, peace in the community, examination malpractice, our environment, health issues (diseases), the computer, cultural practices, the school, election, and child labour and trafficking.
